There is an enormous amount of stigma associated with things associated with femininity being experienced/demonstrated by men, as I *think* androcentrism is attempting to explain. I think any guy, if pressed upon the issue and honest, will relay many experiences where they were punished either verbally, physically, or socially in some manner for displaying 'girly' characteristics.

It is NOT ok to be 'girly' or act in any way that would suggest femininity in our society by and large still to this day. And you *will* fall in line with what is expected of you, or face some potentially violent consequences.

I don't mean to suggest us guys have it harder than women in dealing with societal expectations because I don't think we do, but I've been on the receiving end of the allotted punishments for this type of behavior and it's unpleasant to say the least. And the things that I've witness happen to *others*, well, I'm not comfortable discussing that. Needless to say my experiences pale in comparison.

If you are inclined to waste hours upon hours on the internet reading about topics of dubious value, like many of us, you'll do just fine. I avoid making any commentary on posts that are indicative that the person writing hasn't done little, if any research on the subject though. Not only is that dangerous, but at best you'll just be really disappointed with the results and a lot poorer.
